headers.description: Request headers of an http hook.

matcher.description: A regex over the subject; empty or * matches all.

description: A settings.json, settings.local.json or managed-settings.json file of the app.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, for editors; the app ignores it.

advisorModel.description: Model for the advisor the agent consults.

agent.description: Runs the main conversation as this agent.

bashOutputLimit.description: Characters of a command's output the agent sees; past it, the start and the end are kept and the whole output is saved to a file the agent is pointed to.

disabledMcpServers.description: Project MCP servers you turned off; wins over the approvals.

enableAllProjectMcpServers.description: Starts every MCP server the project's mcp.json declares without asking.

enabledProviders.description: Ids of providers declared by the project that you allow to load.

escalationModel.description: Where a call the agent keeps failing is sent. Read only from your own files.

fallbackModel.description: Model, or chain of models, tried when the chosen one is unavailable.

features.description: Turns features on or off by name.

auto-review.description: When a run changed files, a read-only reviewer checks the changes and the docs before it finishes

branches.description: /branch starts a new conversation from before an earlier prompt, keeping this one

budget.description: /budget stops a session's model calls once it has spent what you allow

cache-warning.description: The status line counts down the prompt cache's last two minutes and says when it has gone cold

channels.description: MCP servers that stay open for the session and send messages to the agent

declared-providers.description: Load the model providers that files in your settings folder and the project declare

destructive-snapshot.description: Before rm -r, git clean, git reset --hard and the like, keep untracked files so /rewind can bring them back

experimental-affected-tests.description: After an edit, run the tests that cover the changed file in the background and tell the agent

experimental-blast-radius.description: After an edit, tell the agent which other files call the symbols it changed (language servers)

experimental-code-map.description: Index the project's symbols and callers with tree-sitter and point each prompt at the matching code

experimental-code-mode.description: REPL becomes the agent's only tool: it writes JavaScript that calls every other tool as a function, and only what the script returns reaches the model

experimental-dependency-guard.description: Before npm, cargo or pip installs a package that is missing, brand new or a typo of a popular one, ask you

experimental-escalation.description: When the agent fails the same call again and again, send it to the Advisor or to escalationModel

experimental-follow-through.description: When an answer ends the turn promising more work ("now I'll run the tests"), a small model checks it and sends the agent back to do it, twice at most

experimental-learning.description: After a run where you corrected the agent, offer one lesson to keep: a memory, a skill or a rule

experimental-learning-check.description: /check has the agent compare the branch's changes with the memories about the files they touch

experimental-load-on-call.description: A tool waiting behind ToolSearch that the agent calls by name is loaded and run, not refused

experimental-memory-anchors.description: Memories name the files they are about, and the agent sees them when it reads or edits those files

experimental-memory-scorecard.description: One request in 20 runs without recalled memory, so /memory score can show whether memory saves corrections and cost

experimental-memory-seed.description: /memory seed offers what you asked for in two or more past sessions as memories to keep

experimental-output-cleanup.description: Bash runs commands without colours and drops escape codes, redrawn progress and repeated lines

experimental-output-filters.description: Bash hides passing tests, build steps and progress from cargo, git, npm, pytest and go test, keeping the whole output in a file

experimental-output-savings.description: /gain shows how much shorter command output reached the model this session

experimental-pr-follow.description: The follow-pr skill watches a pull request and wakes the agent on failing checks and new reviews

experimental-sandbox.description: Confine Bash and Monitor commands to the project's folders (macOS; Linux with Landlock)

experimental-session-claims.description: Warn the agent when another session in the same folder edited the file it is changing

experimental-structured-learnings.description: Decisions are kept as what was decided, what was tried and ruled out, and what to watch out for

experimental-web-cleanup.description: WebFetch drops hidden parts, buttons, links repeated on every item and long runs of menu links

experimental-web-empty-page-error.description: WebFetch reports a page with almost no text (built by JavaScript, a login, a bot check) as an error

experimental-web-formats.description: WebFetch asks for Markdown first and compacts JSON (one line per record) and RSS or Atom feeds

experimental-web-links.description: WebFetch numbers a page's links and lists each address once at the end, same-site ones as paths

experimental-web-main-content.description: WebFetch puts a page's main content first and its menus, header and footer after it

experimental-web-small-pages-direct.description: WebFetch hands a page of 6,000 characters or less to the agent fenced, without the separate reader

git-offer.description: Offer to initialize git on the first message in a folder that is not a repository

memory-search.description: The memory_search tool the agent uses to look further into project memory

plugins.description: Install, update, list and remove plugins

project-criteria.description: Judge every run against the project's checked-in {{DIR}}/verification.md when you set no criteria

redact-secrets.description: Hide tokens, keys and the project's .env values in tool output before the model and the log see them

schedules.description: /loop and /schedules send a prompt again later or on an interval

suggested-rules.description: /rules offers permission rules from answers you keep giving

team-memory.description: Recall the project's checked-in memories in {{DIR}}/memory and share yours there with /memory share <id>

trace.description: /trace and /console show what each run did, on the local web page

hooks.description: Commands, prompts or HTTP calls that run on events.

jsonSchema.description: Gives the agent a StructuredOutput tool whose result must match this JSON Schema.

judgeModel.description: Model for the judge that checks finished work.

lspServers.description: Adds, changes or disables language servers, by name.

outputStyle.description: How the agent talks: a built-in style (default, concise, proactive, explanatory, learning) or the name of a custom style in output-styles/<name>.md.

permissions.description: Allow, ask and deny rules and extra folders.

additionalDirectories.description: Folders the agent reads like the project. Read only from your own files.

allow.description: Tool calls that run without asking. Read only from your own files.

deny.description: Tool calls that are refused, in every mode.

sandbox.description: Where sandboxed commands may write and whether they reach the network.

allowRead.description: Paths sandboxed commands may read on macOS although they are credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gnupg, …) or the app's data folder, which are unreadable by default.

allowUnixSockets.description: Service sockets sandboxed commands may connect to on macOS, such as the Docker socket or a tmux server's (refused by default).

allowWrite.description: Extra folders sandboxed commands may write to.

network.description: false blocks the network for sandboxed commands.

required.description: true refuses commands when the sandbox cannot be provided.

scripts.description: What JavaScript tools, skills, hooks and providers may do.

files.description: Scripts may read and write files.

smallModel.description: Model for background chores: titles, effort picks, web reading.

teammateMode.description: Where a lead starts its teammates: process (in the background, printing to a log), tmux (in a new tmux pane of the window the lead runs in), iterm2 (in a new iTerm2 pane beside the lead) or auto (tmux inside tmux, else iTerm2 inside iTerm2, else process).

trustProjectHooks.description: No longer does anything: a project's hooks run once you trust its folder.

allow.description: Rules the verification judge may run without asking.

title: Settings
